Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **Twelve more transitions** from the extNagano plugin, on every platform: 3duniversal, blurfade, scanline, zoomfade, rgbfade, spin, flutter, book, imagewipe, honeyturn, morphing and multiripple. Use them with `[trans method=...]` or the World's `trans=`; `doc/kagex.txt` ("trans (Extension)") lists their options
- The sample's World Extension: Transition demo ends with all twelve, with rule images of its own for 3duniversal (glass shards) and imagewipe (a brush stroke), and a swirl for morphing. Its seven extrans transitions now show something: they used to go from a picture to the same picture
- A transition whose plugin is missing runs as a crossfade instead of stopping the game
- rgbfade only works between two whole pictures on one layer: on a scene with layers on it, it shows solid colours (a plugin bug, in `UPSTREAM.md`)
- kagex-release keeps rule images lossless when it converts images to JPEG
- kagex-release 0.5.0 downloads the 0.5.0 engines

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.5.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tool aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tool, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
